code: const uint8_t *data = Data; size_t size = Size;
note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes enter the fuzzer harness.

code: int fd = mkstemp(tmpfile); write(fd, data, size);
note: Input bytes are written to a temporary file that will be opened as a RAR archive.
The temporary file is opened as an Archive object for parsing.
Extraction is invoked, which will parse headers and process file data.
PackSize is assembled from unsigned 32-bit fields; in RAR4 format it is always non-negative from parsing.
UnpSize is assembled from unsigned 32-bit fields; also non-negative from parsing.
The PackSize<0 clamp is commented out in this version, but PackSize cannot be negative from header parsing.
UnpSize is still clamped to 0 if negative, but it cannot be negative from parsing either.
UnpPackedSize (uint64) is set from PackSize; since PackSize is non-negative, UnpPackedSize is a normal positive value.
A 1MB (0x100000) heap buffer is allocated for storing uncompressed data.
UnpRead reads up to 1MB from the archive into the buffer; returns the number of bytes actually read.
SizeToRead is the minimum of the requested count and UnpPackedSize; both are positive, so SizeToRead is bounded by 1MB.
File::Read returns at most SizeToRead bytes, so ReadSize cannot exceed the 1MB buffer size.
DestUnpSize is Arc.FileHead.UnpSize which is non-negative and clamped; Code remains bounded by the buffer size.
UnpWrite is called with Code bytes from the 1MB buffer; Code cannot exceed the buffer size.
File::Write reads Count bytes from Addr; since Count is bounded by the 1MB buffer, no out-of-bounds read occurs.
fwrite reads Size bytes from the buffer; with Size bounded by 1MB, this is within the allocated buffer.
